video_title: Matt Barnes & Mad Max REACT to Draymond Green-Dillon Brooks Scuffle

quotes.speaker: Vernon Maxwell
quotes.summary_phrase: Vernon Maxwell criticizes the Rockets' management of Kevin Durant's minutes
quotes.excerpt: I don't like the management shit they talking about they putting on him. That's why I think it's affecting all the shot attempts.
quotes.quote: I don't like the management shit they talking about they putting on him. That's why I think it's affecting all the shot attempts. They said that they didn't want to play him as much in the regular season, so they were going to cut down his minutes in the regular season. I guess they overloaded him last year or some shit, but I don't know if that shit is real.

quotes.speaker: Vernon Maxwell
quotes.summary_phrase: Vernon Maxwell praises Fred VanVleet's impact on the Houston Rockets
quotes.excerpt: You got a real point guard. God knows that's all he did and can shoot it. Smart.
quotes.quote: You got a real point guard. God knows that's all he did and can shoot it. Smart. That's the head of the snake, and he's an extension of Nikola Jokic. Those guys work out together, him and Fred VanVleet, so it's big to have him back. I think that has a lot to do with the Rockets being six and one right now.

quotes.speaker: Matt Barnes
quotes.summary_phrase: Matt Barnes argues Yaxel Lendeborg saved Mike Dunleavy's job
quotes.excerpt: I think Yaxel Lendeborg helps save Mike Dunleavy's job more importantly because Mike didn't really make no moves this off season.
quotes.quote: I think Yaxel Lendeborg helps save Mike Dunleavy's job more importantly because Mike didn't really make no moves this off season. They kind of sat tight. Obviously Kristaps Porzingis is still out with some unknown illnesses. I know Jimmy Butler is scratching at the bit to get back on the court. Yaxel Lendeborg kind of came out of nowhere, respectfully, and has really stepped up into that second scorer role and has completely transformed I think people's thinking about Golden State.

quotes.speaker: Vernon Maxwell
quotes.summary_phrase: Vernon Maxwell expresses concern for Stephen Curry's long-term outlook
quotes.excerpt: Damn, I feel sorry for Stephen Curry, man. It's going to be a long one, boy. God damn.
quotes.quote: Damn, I feel sorry for Stephen Curry, man. It's going to be a long one, boy. God damn. It's going to be a long for my guy, man. Stephen Curry is going to be Stephen Curry, we know that part, but the young guy definitely, he saved Mike Dunleavy's job.

quotes.speaker: Vernon Maxwell
quotes.summary_phrase: Vernon Maxwell demands better production from Draymond Green
quotes.excerpt: Draymond Green has to do better than three points a game. He's making a lot of money now.
quotes.quote: Draymond Green has to do better than three points a game. He's making a lot of money now. God damn now, let's, we got to do better. Three points, five rebounds, six assists. See what I'm saying? He got to do better than that, man.

quotes.speaker: Matt Barnes
quotes.summary_phrase: Matt Barnes calls out Draymond Green for his 'tough guy' act
quotes.excerpt: I think he needs to drop the tough acting and just be a troll because he showed right there.
quotes.quote: I think he needs to drop the tough acting and just be a troll because he showed right there that that tough shit ain't for him, because he had a chance, he had a run at them and Draymond Green turned around and saw red instantly. I think he might have seen the light skin and thought it was Jordan Poole for a second, but Dillon Brooks didn't want no problems with Draymond.

quotes.speaker: Vernon Maxwell
quotes.summary_phrase: Vernon Maxwell criticizes selective toughness in the NBA
quotes.excerpt: What I don't like about that kind of stuff is when you pick and choose who to be tough against.
quotes.quote: What I don't like about that kind of stuff is when you pick and choose who to be tough against. If you're going to be tough in about that stuff, you got to be tough about that stuff with everyone. Always. I don't know how long this stuff going to last for, because like we said, it's a long season.

quotes.speaker: Willie McGinest
quotes.summary_phrase: Willie McGinest praises USC's resilience against Ohio State
quotes.excerpt: I like that the guys didn't give up, you know, regardless. And people are talking about the injuries.
quotes.quote: I like that the guys didn't give up, you know, regardless. And people are talking about the injuries, and what's going on, the starting quarterback then play for Ohio State and all that. But that's part of the game in football. You got to overcome injuries, you got to still play the football game. And I think with all the noise out there after the Wisconsin game and, you know, the guys being down, for them to bounce back against one of the top teams in the nation, I thought it was impressive.

quotes.speaker: Willie McGinest
quotes.summary_phrase: Willie McGinest discusses the parity in college football
quotes.excerpt: There's like 16 teams probably that are six and two, and there's like nine teams that only have one loss.
quotes.quote: There's like 16 teams probably that are six and two, and there's like nine teams that only have one loss outside the top 10. So, there's like, I don't know, 12, 15 teams or more with only one loss or two losses. So, I mean, it's it's tough. That means you basically got to go undefeated to even have a shot. And we're seven and two now.

quotes.speaker: Willie McGinest
quotes.summary_phrase: Willie McGinest advocates for trading for Maxx Crosby
quotes.excerpt: If you need somebody that can whoop ass on the front, go after Maxx Crosby.
quotes.quote: If you need somebody that can whoop ass on the front, go after Maxx Crosby. I think they had interest in him before the season started. The Raiders are trying to build and make moves and collect draft picks to help build that team, and they were willing to trade him before the season. So, hey, Jerry has went all in to me. He's went all in. You might as well go ahead, if you think this is the team, finish it off.

quotes.speaker: Willie McGinest
quotes.summary_phrase: Willie McGinest argues against moving Lamar Jackson
quotes.excerpt: There's a shortage of elite quarterbacks. And if you move Lamar, now you change everything offensively.
quotes.quote: There's a shortage of elite quarterbacks. And if you move Lamar, now you change everything offensively. And it changes everything. And if he goes to another team, if he goes to the right team and he stays healthy, it's trouble. He's a two-time MVP. He's one of the best players in the league. You have to account for him on every play defensively. It's just him staying on the football field. He gives you a chance to win every time he's on the field.

quotes.speaker: Willie McGinest
quotes.summary_phrase: Willie McGinest analyzes Kyler Murray's struggles in the pocket
quotes.excerpt: When I see Kyler Murray, I think he's a good talent. I think he's a talented quarterback.
quotes.quote: When I see Kyler Murray, I think he's a good talent. I think he's a talented quarterback. But here's the problem. Whenever we face quarterbacks like that, we knew that they would get impatient in the pocket from going through progressions because they have talent. They have the ability to run and move the pocket, and they get impatient quick, versus move within the box, they'd rather get out of the box. And we would change our pass rush, call it speed to power, where we push the lineman on top of the quarterback. And if you watch that last game, the majority of the throws he was throwing off his back foot, trying to just throw the ball where he thinks the receiver is going to be. So, that's an issue for me.

quotes.speaker: Willie McGinest
quotes.summary_phrase: Willie McGinest notes Caleb Williams' development in Year 2
quotes.excerpt: When you look at Caleb Williams, he's developed in a year. He was trying to be Superman.
quotes.quote: When you look at Caleb Williams, he's developed in a year. He was trying to be Superman. Now he moves the pocket and he scrambles to throw and allow his receivers to get open. That doesn't happen with Kyler Murray. Kyler Murray is just, he turns into the athlete and then he's taking off where he's trying to improvise and make a play.

quotes.speaker: Willie McGinest
quotes.summary_phrase: Willie McGinest suggests Justin Herbert as a trade target
quotes.excerpt: I heard an interesting trade for Minnesota. Justin Herbert. I heard people talking about that.
quotes.quote: I heard an interesting trade for Minnesota. Justin Herbert. I heard people talking about that. They said he need, if you put Justin Herbert in that system, he can work. Justin Jefferson, you may be talking, you may be talking competing for NFC with that defense, you may be talking about competing for NFC championship. Number Nate, does that make sense?

quotes.speaker: Willie McGinest
quotes.summary_phrase: Willie McGinest emphasizes the need for consistency in receivers
quotes.excerpt: I've seen another receiver like DeAndre Hopkins had like 10 to 11 quarterbacks in his years.
quotes.quote: I've seen another receiver like DeAndre Hopkins had like 10 to 11 quarterbacks in his years while he was playing. Andre Johnson, like there's we we seen guys that still get a thousand yards, still get a number of touchdowns with whoever you put in front of them. So, I think with with a competitive receiver and the talent like that, he just want consistency. He just want somebody back there that can deliver the ball, that he can run routes, the ball is on time, you know, that he can have some cohesiveness with.

quotes.speaker: Willie McGinest
quotes.summary_phrase: Willie McGinest discusses the importance of team balance
quotes.excerpt: It depends on the player. Like we just watched Jeffrey Simmons go crazy. You know, Monday night.
quotes.quote: It depends on the player. Like we just watched Jeffrey Simmons go crazy. You know, Monday night. Went crazy. He had a sack, a number of tackles, tackle for loss. And they gave up what, two first for him? Two first rounds and a fourth round. They gave up a first, a second, a third and Jared Verse for Miles Garrett. They gave up a lot. That's saying we're ready to win now. Like I got all the other pieces and I got young talent that I'm going to have for a few years. So, the draft is not going to give us anything really to change what we got right now. We're ready to go right now.

quotes.speaker: Willie McGinest
quotes.summary_phrase: Willie McGinest reflects on the impact of coaching changes
quotes.excerpt: Yeah, Peyton Manning did it with Denver when he went there. Tom Brady did it when he left.
quotes.quote: Yeah, Peyton Manning did it with Denver when he went there. Tom Brady did it when he left New England and went to Tampa. First year, won a Super Bowl. So, is it more, would you say Von Miller went to Denver, I mean when he left, you know, and and went to Denver like there's a lot of players that it's just one a couple missing pieces, but it has to be at a impactful position. You know, quarterback, linebacker. Obviously, Max Crosby, you spoke on him earlier. Raiders are still trying to figure it out, you know, playing some pretty good football.

quotes.speaker: Willie McGinest
quotes.summary_phrase: Willie McGinest identifies the Buffalo Bills' defensive secondary as a weakness
quotes.excerpt: Buffalo, probably defense secondary. If you want to point out, if you want to nick pick.
quotes.quote: Buffalo, probably defense secondary. If you want to point out, if you want to nick pick. They got to get better. I think when the trade comes, you'll see them probably trade for a defender to help the back end. Because at at some point, you can't get in every game and be in a shootout. And although Josh Allen, this offense is great and they can score points and they can make this miraculous plays, you got to be able to stop people.
